title: Sections with support: the sheaf-level adjunction
statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be admissible (one of the condensed coefficient rings specified in
[sk-def-localizing-closure]), let $X$ be a standing scheme, and let
$i\colon Z\hookrightarrow X$ be a closed immersion with open complement
$j\colon V\hookrightarrow X$. Use $\Lambda_Z=i^{-1}\Lambda_X$ and
$\Lambda_V=j^{-1}\Lambda_X$ as coefficient rings
([sk-def-sfb-coefficient-morphisms]). For
$M\in\Mod(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\Lambda)$ put
$\underline\Gamma_Z(M)=i^*\ker(M\to j_*j^*M)$, where $M\to j_*j^*M$ is the
unit of $j^*\dashv j_*$.

1. $\ker(M\to j_*j^*M)=i_*\underline\Gamma_Z(M)$, naturally in $M$.
2. $\underline\Gamma_Z\colon\Mod(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\Lambda)\to\Mod(Z_{\mathrm{proét}},\Lambda)$
   is right adjoint to the exact functor
   $i_*\colon\Mod(Z_{\mathrm{proét}},\Lambda)\to\Mod(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\Lambda)$;
   in particular it is left exact and preserves limits.
3. $\underline\Gamma_Z$ sends K-injective complexes to K-injective complexes,
   and injective modules to injective modules.

proof.text: Finite type over the field makes X locally Noetherian; quasi-compactness over Spec k makes X compact. Thus X is Noetherian, and the open immersion j is quasi-compact. Apply abelian_closed_support to obtain the actual abelian closed counit and invertibility of the actual closed unit on sheaves vanishing on the open complement.

Lift the abelian closed counit and supported closed unit to internal modules through the mapMod adjunction and the scalar-change equivalence for the coefficient isomorphism. The faithful module forgetful functor reflects isomorphisms. The canonical profinitePointModuleForgetPullbackIso transfers vanishing of the module inverse image to vanishing of the abelian inverse image. Closed direct image is consequently fully faithful.

For every module on Z, its closed direct image has zero open restriction: on a pro-etale object of V, base change to Z is empty, and a sheaf has zero sections on the empty scheme. Transfer this vanishing through the module forgetful comparison. The abelian open restriction/direct-image counit is invertible (the declaration attached to def-sfb-finite-lower-shriek-to-lower-star). Consequently the abelian open direct image is fully faithful, so the counit of the canonical abelian inverse-image adjunction is invertible too. Apply the same mapMod and scalar-change counit lifting used for the closed immersion to obtain the module open counit. No module extension by zero or projection formula is used.

The two exact inverse images jointly detect zero modules: if the open image vanishes, the supported closed unit identifies the module with the closed direct image of its closed inverse image. To prove closed direct image right exact, apply both inverse images to the cokernel of a pushed-forward epimorphism. Closed restriction identifies the map with the original epimorphism via the invertible counit; open restriction has zero target. Both cokernel restrictions vanish, so the cokernel is zero. The additive closed direct image preserves epimorphisms and kernels, hence homology and finite colimits. Its preservation of finite limits is already an instance.

Let S be the kernel of the open unit in the functor category. Evaluation preserves kernels, so S(M) canonically identifies with the kernel of the unit component. Applying exact open inverse image gives zero, since the triangle identity and invertible open counit make the image of the unit invertible. The supported closed unit is therefore invertible on every S(M); its naturality gives the canonical isomorphism S ≅ S ⋙ i^* ⋙ i_*. For a map i_*B → M, its composite with the open unit is zero by the open adjunction and the vanishing of j^*i_*B. Factor it through the evaluated kernel, use its comparison with S(M), and apply the closed unit. Full faithfulness of i_* supplies the unique map B → i^*S(M). The inverse uses the inverse supported unit and kernel inclusion. Cancellation against these monomorphisms proves injectivity; kernel lifting proves surjectivity; naturality follows from the natural counit given by the inverse supported unit followed by kernel inclusion. This constructs the adjunction to exactly the stated functor, without replacing its kernel definition.

The right adjoint of the additive closed direct image is additive. Its constructed adjunction gives preservation of every small limit in the specified universes, and hence finite limits. Since closed direct image preserves monomorphisms, Adjunction.map_injective gives preservation of injective modules.

Apply the proved Adjunction.preservesKInjectiveComplexes in WeilConjectures.CategoryTheory.DerivedCategory.RightDerivedFunctor.Comp. This is the termwise adjunction argument of clause (3): the exact left adjoint maps acyclic complexes to acyclic complexes, and a map from such a complex into the right-adjoint image transposes to a map into the original K-injective. Its zero homotopy transfers back termwise. Thus every unbounded K-injective has K-injective image. No separate adjunction on homotopy categories is required.

split_report.summary: Split the existing three-clause sheaf theorem into seven checked steps, reusing arbitrary-ring-sheaf recollement and generic categorical tools. No new nodes. Replaced a dangling Cartesian-coefficients reference by the existing coefficient-morphism isomorphism statement; preserved the hypotheses and conclusions. Made the actual open counit, kernel naturality, the two directions of the Hom bijection, and unbounded K-injectivity explicit. Existing project Lean covers only the constant-ring adjunction, not all clauses for condensed admissible coefficients.
